title: Bangladesh Stun Australia Early as WTC Standings Battle Intensifies for India
excerpt: Bangladesh's pace attack reduced Australia to 74-4 at lunch on Day 1 of the first Test in Darwin, a result that could reshape the World Test Championship race India is desperately trying to stay in.
body:
• Bangladesh bowled Australia out of their top order, leaving the hosts at 74-4 at lunch on Day 1 in Darwin
  • Hasan Mahmud dismissed both Australian openers while Ebadot Hossain removed Marnus Labuschagne for 1
  • The two-Test series carries WTC 2025-27 cycle points, with Australia leading at 87.5% and India's qualification hopes hanging by a thread
  • Any Australian stumble in this series could crack open the WTC standings and give India a narrow path back into contention

Bangladesh's depleted pace attack delivered a stunning opening salvo against Australia on Day 1 of the first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin on Thursday, reducing the hosts to 74 for four at lunch and injecting fresh uncertainty into the World Test Championship standings.

Bangladesh's Pacers Dismantle Australia's Top Order

Australia captain Pat Cummins won the toss and elected to bat on a grassy pitch under hot Northern Territory skies, but his top order crumbled against disciplined fast bowling. Hasan Mahmud was the chief destroyer, removing both openers — Jake Weatherald, who edged a loose drive to the slips for 23, and Travis Head, who chopped onto his stumps.

Ebadot Hossain added to Australia's misery by dismissing Marnus Labuschagne for just one, while Taskin Ahmed accounted for Cameron Green, caught at short midwicket for 13. Steve Smith survived on seven not out, having been dropped on two in the slips off Ebadot's bowling.

"We're delighted to bring Test cricket to northern Australia and look forward to a fantastic series against Bangladesh."

— Todd Greenberg, Cricket Australia CEO

Why This Series Matters for India's WTC Hopes

The series is part of the WTC 2025-27 cycle, and every result carries weight for India's fading championship ambitions. Australia sit atop the standings with a dominant 87.5% points percentage from seven wins in eight matches. Bangladesh occupy fourth place at 58.33%.

India, meanwhile, have endured a torrid run in Test cricket under head coach Gautam Gambhir — seven wins, 10 losses, and two draws across 19 Tests. Series defeats to New Zealand (3-0), Australia (3-1), and South Africa (2-0) have left India's WTC qualification prospects precarious.

If Bangladesh can pull off an upset or even draw a Test, it would deny Australia maximum points and potentially keep the door open for India. Conversely, a clean Australian sweep would further cement their grip on the top spot and narrow India's already slim margin for error in their remaining fixtures.

Historic Return to Darwin

The match marks Bangladesh's first Test series in Australia since 2003, and Darwin's first Test since hosting Sri Lanka in 2004. The second Test will be played at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay from August 22-26, making it the venue's first-ever Test match.

Bangladesh enter the series as heavy underdogs — Australia have won five of six Tests between the sides historically, with Bangladesh's only win coming in Mirpur in 2017. A warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI in Darwin ended in an innings defeat for the tourists, though Mehidy Hasan Miraz scored a defiant century.

What's Next

The afternoon session will test whether Australia's middle order, led by Smith and all-rounder Cameron Green's replacement, can rebuild. For Indian fans, this series is appointment viewing — not for the teams on the field, but for the points at stake. Every run and every wicket in Darwin carries implications for whether India can mount a late WTC charge or watch Australia pull further away at the top of the championship table.
nri_angle: India's WTC qualification hopes hinge on results in this series, as Australian dominance could further diminish India's chances of reaching the championship final.
